First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{3x-1} & ={6}^{2x+1} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{3x-1}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({6}^{2x+1})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{a})=a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

$$
3x-1=\operatorname{ln}⁡({6}^{2x+1}).
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
3x-1=(2x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x-1 & =(2x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡(6) \\ 3x-1 & =2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(6) \\ 3x-2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(6) & =1+\operatorname{ln}⁡(6) \\ x(3-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)) & =1+\operatorname{ln}⁡(6) \\ x & =\frac{1+\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)}{3-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)}\end{aligned}
$$
